title: Hausa
motto: The major Afroasiatic trade language spoken by 80M+ people across West & Central Africa.
description: Discover Hausa with trans-Saharan trade warmth, royal Emirates greetings, and market eloquence.

proverbOfDay.proverb: Komi ya yi nisa, zai dawo kusa.
proverbOfDay.translation: However far a journey or circumstance goes, it will eventually return near.
proverbOfDay.context: A proverb counseling patience, endurance, and knowing that events run full circles.

slangs.example: Sannu da aiki! (Well done with your work!)
Sai an jima, mu kwana lafiya.

cultureTips.title: The Respectful 'Gaisuwa' Salutation
cultureTips.description: In Hausa culture, greetings are comprehensive and cordial, inquiring about health ('lafiya'), family, and work before moving to any business.

cultureTips.title: Trans-Saharan Trade Heritage
cultureTips.description: Hausa has functioned as the primary mercantile language across West and Central Africa from Niger to Cameroon for over seven centuries.

customUnits.title: Unit 1: The Hausa Alphabet and Vowels (Bakaken Da Wasula)
customUnits.subtitle: Consonants, hook letters (ɓ, ɗ, ƙ, ʼy), glottal stop, vowel length, and tonal drills.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Boko Orthography, Hook Letters & Tonal System
lessons.description: Master standard Hausa Latin (Boko) characters, unique hooked consonants, and short vs. long vowel distinctions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a special hooked consonant (bàƙin ƙirƙira) in the Hausa Boko alphabet?
questions.explanation: Hausa features distinctive implosive and ejective consonants written with hooked letters: Ɓ/ɓ, Ɗ/ɗ, Ƙ/ƙ, and ʼY/ʼy.

questions.prompt: Match the Hausa hooked letter with its phonetic description:

questions.sentence: In Hausa, vowel length changes meaning: 'fari' means white, while 'faari' means ___.
questions.explanation: Vowel length is phonemic in Hausa: short vowel 'fari' (white) contrasts with long vowel 'faari' (drought/famine).

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Hausa alphabet has vowels' (Bakaken Hausa suna da wasula):
Listen to the word with the hooked consonant 'Ɓ'. What does 'Ɓarawo' mean?
questions.phrase: Ɓarawo
questions.explanation: 'Ɓarawo' (thief/robber) begins with the voiced bilabial implosive Ɓ.

questions.prompt: How many primary vowels exist in standard Hausa phonology?
questions.explanation: Hausa has 5 basic vowel qualities (a, e, i, o, u), each occurring in phonemic short and long variants.

questions.prompt: What is the Hausa term for the Latin script used to write modern Hausa?
questions.explanation: 'Boko' refers to the Latin orthography officially adopted for Hausa in the early 20th century.

questions.prompt: Match the Hausa linguistic terms with their English meanings:

questions.sentence: The word 'ɗa' (with hooked ɗ) means ___ in Hausa.
questions.explanation: 'Ɗa' means son or child, distinct from plain 'da' which functions as the preposition 'with / and'.

questions.prompt: Which tones are systematically present in Hausa speech work?
options: High tone, Low tone, and Falling tone
High tone and Click tone only
questions.correctAnswer: High tone, Low tone, and Falling tone
questions.explanation: Hausa is a tonal language utilizing High (á), Low (à), and Falling (â) tones that distinguish word meanings and grammatical aspects.

questions.prompt: What does the glottal consonant 'Ƙ' represent in a word like 'ƙofa'?
questions.explanation: 'Ƙofa' (door / entrance / gate) begins with the ejective velar consonant Ƙ.

questions.prompt: Match the Hausa word with its hooked initial letter:

questions.sentence: The letter 'ʼy' in 'ʼyaʼya' represents the sound for ___.
questions.explanation: 'ʼYaʼya' translates to children or fruits, featuring the glottalized 'ʼy' digraph.

questions.prompt: In Hausa phonology, diphthongs include which of the following pairs?
questions.explanation: Standard Hausa features two primary diphthongs: 'ai' (as in 'kai' - head) and 'au' (as in 'sau' - times/footprint).

questions.prompt: Arrange the tokens to form: 'Kai ne abokina' (You are my friend):
Listen to the phrase. What does 'Manya da ƙanana' mean?
questions.phrase: Manya da ƙanana
questions.explanation: 'Manya' (adults/great ones) and 'ƙanana' (little ones/children) is a common inclusive social phrase.

questions.prompt: Which pair demonstrates that tone alone changes meaning in Hausa?
options: fàrī (high tone on ri = drought) vs fárì (low tone on ri = white)
questions.correctAnswer: fàrī (high tone on ri = drought) vs fárì (low tone on ri = white)
questions.explanation: Tone is lexical in Hausa: identical spelling can yield completely different words based on high and low pitches.

questions.sentence: When writing long vowels in standard educational linguistic transcription, the vowel is written ___.
questions.explanation: In linguistic texts, vowel length is marked by doubling the letter (aa, ee, ii, oo, uu) or using a macron (ā).

questions.prompt: What sound does the apostrophe (hamza) represent in words like 'aʼa' (no)?
questions.explanation: The apostrophe represents the glottal stop (hamza), a distinct consonant produced by closing the vocal cords.

questions.prompt: Match the vowel types with their example words:

customUnits.title: Unit 2: Greetings and Social Courtesies (Gaisuwa)
customUnits.subtitle: Time-of-day salutations, formal honorifics, and Islamic-cultural courtesy responses.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Gaisuwar Hausa & Respectful Salutations
lessons.description: Master daily greetings from morning to night and formal courtesies like Ranki ya dade.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'Good morning' in Hausa?
questions.explanation: 'Ina kwana?' (How did you sleep?) and 'Barka da safiya' (Blessings of the morning) are the standard morning salutations.

questions.prompt: Match the Hausa greetings with their time of day:

questions.sentence: When someone asks 'Ina kwana?', the polite answer is '___' (In good peace).
questions.explanation: 'Lafiya lau' (in perfect peace/health) is the universal respectful response to greeting inquiries.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'May your life be prolonged' (Royal/Formal title):
Listen to the audio. What does 'Sannu da aiki' mean?
questions.phrase: Sannu da aiki
questions.explanation: 'Sannu da aiki' is warmly used to greet anyone currently working or performing tasks.

questions.prompt: What is the respectful greeting addressed specifically to an esteemed woman or mother?
questions.explanation: 'Hajiya' or 'Iya' expresses deep honor and filial courtesy towards an elder woman or mother.

questions.prompt: What does 'Yaya kake?' mean when greeting someone?
questions.explanation: 'Yaya kake?' asks 'How are you?' to a male, while 'Yaya kike?' is used when addressing a female.

questions.prompt: Match the gendered Hausa greeting phrases:

questions.sentence: To express sincere gratitude in Hausa, one says '___' (Thank you very much).
questions.explanation: 'Nagode' means thank you; adding 'sosai' intensifies it to 'thank you very much'.

questions.prompt: What is the common parting phrase meaning 'Until later / Goodbye'?
questions.explanation: 'Sai an jima' means 'Until later' or 'See you in a bit', signaling a warm departure.

questions.prompt: If you are leaving someone until tomorrow, what do you say?
questions.explanation: 'Sai gobe' literally means 'Until tomorrow' ('gobe' = tomorrow).

questions.prompt: Match the courtesy responses with their English meanings:

questions.sentence: When a guest enters the home, the host warmly says '___' (Welcome!).
questions.explanation: 'Barka da zuwa' is the premier welcoming formula for visitors and travelers.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'How is the tiredness?' (Ina gajiya?):
How does one reply to 'Ina gajiya?' (How is the fatigue/tiredness)?
questions.explanation: Politeness dictates minimizing fatigue by cheerfully responding 'Babu gajiya' (No tiredness / We are energized).

questions.prompt: Listen to the blessing. What does 'Allah ya ba da sa'a' mean?
questions.phrase: Allah ya ba da sa'a
options: May God grant success / good fortune
questions.correctAnswer: May God grant success / good fortune
questions.explanation: 'Allah ya ba da sa'a' is a traditional prayer/benediction wishing someone divine favor and triumph.

questions.prompt: What does 'Barka da hutawa' mean?
options: Happy relaxing / Happy weekend or rest!
questions.correctAnswer: Happy relaxing / Happy weekend or rest!
questions.explanation: 'Hutawa' means resting; 'Barka da hutawa' wishes someone a refreshing rest or holiday.

questions.sentence: The phrase 'Don Allah' is used to politely say '___'.
questions.explanation: 'Don Allah' (for the sake of God) is the customary polite term for 'please'.

questions.prompt: What is the polite title for an Islamic scholar, respected teacher, or gentleman?
questions.explanation: 'Mallam' (from Arabic mu'allim) is the distinguished title for teachers, scholars, and gentlemen.

questions.prompt: Match the traditional Hausa titles with their roles:

customUnits.title: Unit 3: Numbers, Colors, and Days (Lambar Lamba da Launuka)
customUnits.subtitle: Counting 1 to 50, basic chromatic terms, and the seven days of the week.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Ƙidaya, Ranaku da Launuka
lessons.description: Master counting from 1 to 50, days from Litinin to Lahadi, and core descriptive colors.

questions.prompt: What is the Hausa number for 'One' and 'Two'?
questions.explanation: In Hausa: 1 = Ɗaya, 2 = Biyu.

questions.prompt: Match the Hausa numerals from 1 to 5:

questions.sentence: The number 5 in Hausa is '___', and 10 is 'goma'.
questions.explanation: 1 to 5: ɗaya, biyu, uku, huɗu, biyar. 10 is goma.

questions.prompt: Arrange the numbers in order from 6 to 8 (Shida, Bakwai, Takwas):
Listen to the number. What is 'Ashirin da biyar'?
questions.phrase: Ashirin da biyar
questions.explanation: 'Ashirin' = 20, 'da biyar' = and five, totaling 25.

questions.prompt: What is the Hausa word for 'Twenty' and 'Thirty'?
questions.explanation: Tens: 10 = Goma, 20 = Ashirin, 30 = Talatin, 40 = Arba'in, 50 = Hamsin.

questions.prompt: What is the Hausa number for 50?
questions.explanation: 50 is 'Hamsin', derived from the Afroasiatic/Arabic root for five.

questions.prompt: Match the primary Hausa colors with their English equivalents:

questions.sentence: The color yellow is called '___' in Hausa.
questions.explanation: 'Rawaya' is the standard Hausa term for the color yellow.

questions.prompt: What color is 'shudi' in Hausa?
questions.explanation: 'Shudi' represents blue, often associated with sky and traditional indigo dye.

questions.prompt: Which day of the week is 'Ranar Litinin'?
questions.explanation: 'Litinin' corresponds to Monday (from the Arabic root al-Ithnayn).

questions.prompt: Match the Hausa days of the week:

questions.sentence: The sacred Muslim congregational prayer day on Friday is called 'Ranar ___'.
questions.explanation: Friday is 'Ranar Juma'a', the day of the weekly Friday congregational prayer.

questions.prompt: Arrange the weekend days: 'Saturday and Sunday' (Asabar da Lahadi):
Listen to the phrase. What does 'Kwanaki bakwai a mako' mean?
questions.phrase: Kwanaki bakwai a mako
questions.explanation: 'Kwanaki' = days, 'bakwai' = seven, 'a mako' = in a week.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'Forty' in Hausa?
questions.explanation: 40 is 'Arba'in'.

questions.prompt: What does 'Yau wace rana ce?' ask?
questions.explanation: 'Yau wace rana ce?' translates directly to 'What day is today?' ('yau' = today).

questions.sentence: To say 'Tomorrow is Wednesday', you say: 'Gobe Ranar ___ ce'.
questions.explanation: 'Laraba' is Wednesday.

questions.prompt: What is 'Ɗari' in Hausa numbering?
questions.explanation: 'Ɗari' = 100, while 'Dubu' = 1,000.

questions.prompt: Match the complex numerals with their digits:

customUnits.title: Unit 4: Family and Home (Iyali da Gida)
customUnits.subtitle: Kinship nomenclature, domestic living spaces, furniture, and household objects.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Iyalin Hausa & Sashen Gida
lessons.description: Learn words for immediate family relations (Uba, Uwa, Dan) and domestic household spaces.

questions.prompt: What is the Hausa word for 'Father'?
questions.explanation: 'Uba' is the formal term for father, commonly addressed colloquially as 'Baba'.

questions.prompt: Match the immediate nuclear family members:

questions.sentence: Grandmother or grandfather in Hausa is called '___'.
questions.explanation: 'Kaka' is the reciprocal term for grandparent.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'This is my home' (Wannan gida na ne):
Listen to the phrase. What does it describe?
questions.phrase: Babban yaya da ƙani
questions.explanation: 'Yaya' = older sibling, 'ƙani' = younger brother.

questions.prompt: What is the Hausa word for 'Younger sister'?
questions.explanation: 'Ƙanwa' is younger sister, while 'ƙani' is younger brother.

questions.prompt: What is the kitchen called in a traditional Hausa household?
questions.explanation: 'Ɗakin girki' literally means 'room of cooking' (kitchen).

questions.prompt: Match the rooms and spaces of a Hausa house:

questions.sentence: The entrance room where visitors are formally received is called the '___'.
questions.explanation: The 'zaure' is the cultural entrance porch where guests are greeted to preserve household privacy.

questions.prompt: What is a 'kujera'?
questions.explanation: 'Kujera' means chair, borrowed from Arabic 'kursi'.

questions.prompt: What does 'gado' mean in a bedroom context?
questions.explanation: 'Gado' translates to bed.

questions.prompt: Match household furniture and items:

questions.sentence: A traditional grass or plastic woven mat used for sitting and prayer is called '___'.
questions.explanation: 'Tabarma' is the ubiquitous mat found in Northern homes for sitting and hospitality.

questions.prompt: Arrange the tokens to form: 'Mahaifina yana gida' (My father is at home):
What is the Hausa term for maternal uncle?
questions.explanation: 'Kawu' is the maternal uncle, while 'Baffa' refers to the paternal uncle.

questions.prompt: Listen to the host's greeting. What does it mean?
questions.phrase: Barka da zuwa gidanmu
options: Please sit down on the chair!
questions.explanation: 'Gidanmu' means 'our house/home'.

questions.prompt: What is 'Tagari / Taga' in a room?
questions.explanation: 'Taga' is the window.

questions.sentence: The door or entrance gate of a house is called '___'.
questions.explanation: 'Ƙofa' means door or portal.

questions.prompt: What is 'makwabci'?
questions.explanation: 'Makwabci' is the neighbor; good neighborliness ('makwabtaka') is deeply valued in Hausa culture.

questions.prompt: Match extended kinship terms:

customUnits.title: Unit 5: Basic Action Verbs and Commands (Ayyuka)
customUnits.subtitle: High-frequency verbs of motion, consumption, state, and imperative commands.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Fi'ili & Umarni (Verbs & Imperatives)
lessons.description: Master foundational verbs (zo, tafi, ci, sha) and construct immediate action commands.

questions.prompt: What does the action verb 'Zo' mean in Hausa?
questions.explanation: 'Zo' is the imperative/verb meaning 'Come' (e.g., 'Zo nan' = Come here).

questions.prompt: Match the basic Hausa verbs of movement and action:

questions.sentence: The command 'Zo ___' means 'Come here'.
questions.explanation: 'Nan' = here, so 'Zo nan!' means 'Come here!'.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to command: 'Tafi gida yanzu' (Go home now):
Listen to the instruction. What is the listener asked to do?
questions.phrase: Zauna a kan kujera
questions.explanation: 'Zauna' = sit down; 'a kan kujera' = upon the chair.

questions.prompt: What does 'Tashi' mean when instructing someone?
questions.explanation: 'Tashi' means to stand up, rise, or wake up.

questions.prompt: What is the verb for 'To read' in Hausa?
questions.explanation: 'Karanta' means to read or study.

questions.prompt: Match the literacy and sensory verbs:

questions.sentence: To command someone to 'Listen carefully', one says: '___ da kyau'.
questions.explanation: 'Ji' means hear/listen; 'da kyau' = well/carefully.

questions.prompt: What is the verb for 'To wash' in 'Wanke hannu' (Wash your hands)?
questions.explanation: 'Wanke' means to wash with water.

questions.prompt: What does 'Bude kofa' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Bude' = open; 'kofa' = door.

questions.prompt: Match opposite imperative commands:

questions.sentence: To tell someone 'Do not go!', you use the negative imperative particle: '___ tafi!'.
questions.explanation: 'Kada ka' (to a male) or 'Kada ki' (to a female) forms the negative command 'Do not'.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Ci abinci yanzu' (Eat food now):
What is 'Kawo ruwa'?
questions.explanation: 'Kawo' means bring/fetch.

questions.prompt: Listen to the command. What does 'Tsaya a nan' mean?
questions.phrase: Tsaya a nan
questions.explanation: 'Tsaya' = stop/wait; 'a nan' = right here.

questions.prompt: What does 'Gudu' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Gudu' means to run or flee.

questions.sentence: When asking someone to give you something, you say: '___ mini' (Give me).
questions.explanation: 'Ba' is the verb 'give'; 'Ba ni' or 'Ba mini' = give me.

questions.prompt: What does 'Koyi' mean in an educational setting?
questions.explanation: 'Koyi' means to learn, while 'koyar' means to teach.

questions.prompt: Match transactional and cooperative verbs:

customUnits.title: Unit 6: Pronouns and Possessives (Wakilan Suna)
customUnits.subtitle: Subject pronouns, independent vs. pronominal affixes, and expressing possession with nawa/naka/nata.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Wakilan Suna da Mallaka (Pronouns & Ownership)
lessons.description: Master Hausa independent pronouns, person-aspect prefixes, and possessive suffixes (-na, -ka, -ki, -sa, -ta).

questions.prompt: What is the Hausa independent first-person singular pronoun ('I / me')?
questions.explanation: 'Ni' is the independent pronoun for 'I/me'. 'Kai' is 'you (male)', 'Shi' is 'he', and 'Mu' is 'we'.

questions.prompt: Match independent Hausa pronouns with their English equivalents:

questions.sentence: To say 'This book is mine', you say: 'Wannan littafi ___ ne'.
questions.explanation: 'Nawa' means 'mine' for a masculine noun (littafi). 'Tawa' would be used for a feminine noun.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Mu ne dalibai' (We are students):
Listen to the phrase. What does 'Wannan motar tawa ce' mean?
questions.phrase: Wannan motar tawa ce
questions.explanation: 'Mota' is feminine, so the feminine possessive 'tawa' and stabilizer 'ce' are used: 'Wannan motar tawa ce'.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'your house' speaking to a male?
questions.explanation: The masculine possessive suffix attached to a masculine noun is '-nka': 'Gidanka'.

questions.prompt: Match the attached possessive forms (masculine noun root 'Gida'):

questions.sentence: The independent pronoun for 'They / them' in Hausa is '___'.
questions.explanation: 'Su' means 'they' or 'them', while 'Ku' is plural 'you all'.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Kudi naku ne' (The money is yours [plural]):
Which pair shows the difference between masculine 'ne' and feminine 'ce' stabilization?
questions.explanation: In Hausa, 'ne' stabilizes masculine nouns (littafi ne), and 'ce' stabilizes feminine nouns (hula ce).

questions.prompt: Listen to the question. What does 'Wa ya kira ni?' ask?
questions.phrase: Wa ya kira ni?
questions.explanation: 'Wa' = who; 'ya kira' = he called; 'ni' = me: 'Who called me?'.

questions.prompt: Match plural subject pronouns with English meanings:

questions.sentence: When asking 'Whose pencil is this?', you say: 'Alkalami na ___ ne wannan?'.
questions.explanation: 'Na wa' means 'whose' (literally: of whom); 'wa' means who.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Ita ce kawata' (She is my friend [female]):
What is the meaning of 'Namu ne'?
questions.explanation: 'Namu' = ours; 'Namu ne' = It is ours.

questions.prompt: Listen to the phrase. What does 'Wannan babban gidan nasu ne' mean?
questions.phrase: Wannan babban gidan nasu ne
questions.explanation: 'Gidan nasu' = their house; 'Wannan babban gidan nasu ne' = This big house is theirs.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'My father' in Hausa using possessive suffixing?
questions.explanation: '-na' attached to Uba/Baba signifies first person singular: 'Ubana' or 'Babana' = my father.

questions.sentence: For feminine possession, 'tawa' means 'mine', while '___' means 'hers'.
questions.explanation: 'Tata' is the feminine independent possessive pronoun for 'hers'.

questions.prompt: What does 'Ku saurara' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Ku' is 2nd person plural, and 'saurara' means listen: 'You all listen!'.

questions.prompt: Match demonstrative pronouns with their meanings:

customUnits.title: Unit 7: Time, Seasons, and Weather (Lokaci da Yanayi)
customUnits.subtitle: Dry season (Rani), rainy season (Damina), harmattan (Kaka/Bazara), telling time, and daily routines.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Lokaci, Yanayi da Yanayin Rana (Time & Meteorology)
lessons.description: Learn the agricultural seasons of Northern Nigeria, telling clock time, and describing meteorological conditions.

questions.prompt: What is the Hausa term for the rainy season?
questions.explanation: 'Damina' is the rainy/wet farming season, whereas 'Rani' is the dry season.

questions.prompt: Match the Northern Nigerian ecological seasons:

pairs.english: Hot transition season just before rain

questions.sentence: To say 'It is two o'clock', you say: 'Karfe ___ ne'.
questions.explanation: 'Karfe biyu' literally translates to 'clock two' (two o'clock).

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Ana ruwa sosai yau' (It is raining heavily today):
Listen to the weather report. What does 'Yau akwai zafi sosai' mean?
questions.phrase: Yau akwai zafi sosai
questions.explanation: 'Zafi' means heat; 'Yau akwai zafi sosai' = Today is very hot.

questions.prompt: What is the Hausa word for 'cold' (temperature/weather)?
questions.explanation: 'Sanyi' means cold or chill, prominent during the harmattan season.

questions.prompt: Match clock time phrases:

questions.sentence: Dusty harmattan haze typical of the northern dry season is known as '___'.
questions.explanation: 'Hazo' refers to fog, haze, or the harmattan dust shroud.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Karfe shida na safe' (Six o'clock in the morning):
What does 'Tsawa' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Tsawa' is thunder; 'walkiya' is lightning.

questions.prompt: Listen to the phrase. What does 'Rana ta fito' mean?
questions.phrase: Rana ta fito
options: The sun has risen / come out
questions.correctAnswer: The sun has risen / come out
questions.explanation: 'Rana' = sun/day; 'fito' = emerge: 'The sun has risen / come out'.

questions.prompt: Match parts of the 24-hour cycle:

questions.sentence: When asking what time it is, you ask: 'Karfe ___ ne yanzu?'.
questions.explanation: 'Karfe nawa ne yanzu?' translates to 'What time is it now?'.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Dare ya yi' (Night has fallen):
What is 'Wata' in the context of time and astronomy?
questions.explanation: 'Wata' signifies both the moon and a calendar month.

questions.prompt: Listen to the phrase. What natural phenomenon does 'guguwa' describe?
questions.phrase: Iskanci da guguwa na kadawa
questions.explanation: 'Guguwa' means a whirlwind or dust storm in Hausa.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'Last year' in Hausa?
questions.explanation: 'Bara' = last year; 'Bana' = this year; 'Badi' = next year.

questions.sentence: To say 'this year', the Hausa expression is '___'.
questions.explanation: 'Bana' is this year; 'Bara' was last year.

questions.prompt: What does 'Hadari' signify when looking at the sky?
questions.explanation: 'Hadari' refers to a gathering rainstorm or threatening storm clouds.

questions.prompt: Match temporal adverbs:

customUnits.title: Unit 8: Market and Shopping (A Kasuwa)
customUnits.subtitle: Currency, food provisions, bargaining vocabulary, and authentic commerce dialogues.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Kasuwanci, Ciniki da Siyayya (Market & Bargaining)
lessons.description: Navigate open-air markets, negotiate prices politely, purchase staples, and handle Nigerian currency.

questions.prompt: How do you ask 'How much is this?' in a Hausa market?
questions.explanation: 'Nawa ne kudin wannan?' directly asks 'How much is the cost of this?'.

questions.prompt: Match market food items with English translations:

questions.sentence: When the price is too high and you want a discount, you say: 'Don Allah ___ min kudi'.
questions.explanation: 'Rage min kudi' means 'Reduce the price/money for me'.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Wannan ya yi tsada sosai' (This is too expensive):
Listen to the buyer. What offer is being made?
questions.phrase: Zan ba ka Naira dari biyar
options: I want to sell for 200 Naira
questions.explanation: 'Naira dari biyar' = 500 Naira ('dari' = 100, 'biyar' = 5).

questions.prompt: What does 'Ciniki' mean in Hausa culture?
questions.explanation: 'Ciniki' refers to trade, bargaining, or doing business.

questions.prompt: Match cooking ingredients sold at kasuwa:

questions.sentence: The general Hausa word for 'money' is '___'.
questions.explanation: 'Kudi' is money or currency.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Ina son in sayi nama' (I want to buy meat):
What does 'Mai shago' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Mai shago' translates to the owner/operator of a shop (shago).

questions.prompt: Listen to the customer. What are they requesting?
questions.phrase: Ina canjin kudi na?
questions.explanation: 'Canji' means change/balance from a cash transaction.

questions.prompt: Match market roles and locations:

questions.sentence: If an item is cheap and affordable, you say: 'Wannan yana da ___' (It is cheap).
questions.explanation: 'Sauki' means easiness or cheapness/affordability.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Kasuwa tana cike da mutane' (The market is full of people):
What is a 'Mudu' in traditional markets across Northern Nigeria?
options: A standardized grain bowl measuring unit
questions.correctAnswer: A standardized grain bowl measuring unit
questions.explanation: A 'mudu' is a widespread dry-measure bowl used to sell grains like rice, millet, and beans.

questions.prompt: Listen to the order. What is the customer buying?
questions.phrase: Bani mudu biyu na shinkafa
questions.explanation: 'Mudu biyu na shinkafa' = two mudu measures of rice.

questions.prompt: What does 'Aljihu' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Aljihu' is pocket (where one puts money or small belongings).

questions.sentence: When asking to weigh or measure something, you use the verb '___' (to measure/weigh).
questions.explanation: 'Auna' means to weigh or measure (volume/weight).

questions.prompt: If a merchant says 'Babu riba', what does he claim?
options: There is no profit in this price
questions.correctAnswer: There is no profit in this price
questions.explanation: 'Riba' means profit; 'Babu riba' is a classic bargaining phrase meaning 'There is no profit left'.

questions.prompt: Match monetary denominations and terms:

questions.prompt: Which marker indicates the continuous (progressive) aspect for a 3rd person masculine subject ('he is doing')?
questions.explanation: 'Yana' denotes progressive/continuous aspect for 3rd person masculine ('Yana tafiya' = He is walking).

questions.prompt: Match the 3rd person masculine aspectual pronoun markers:

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Sun tafi makaranta da safe' (They went to school in the morning):

questions.phrase: Ina aiki a asibiti amma ina zaune a gida
questions.explanation: 'Amma' means 'but' and introduces a contrasting clause.

questions.prompt: Which conjunction means 'because' or 'in order that' in Hausa?
questions.explanation: 'Domin' and 'Saboda' both mean 'because / in order to'.

questions.prompt: Match Hausa coordinating and subordinating conjunctions:

questions.sentence: To say 'After we ate, we slept', you say: '___ mun ci abinci, muka kwanta'.
questions.explanation: 'Bayan' means 'after' in narrative sequencing.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Zan tafi gida saboda na gaji' (I will go home because I am tired):

questions.explanation: 'Bai ... ba' is the discontinuous negative completive/past marker for 3rd person masculine.

questions.prompt: Listen to the sentence. What tense/aspect and polarity is expressed?
questions.phrase: Ba za su zo ba gobe
options: Negative future ('They will not come tomorrow')
questions.correctAnswer: Negative future ('They will not come tomorrow')
questions.explanation: 'Ba za su ... ba' indicates negative future: 'They will not come tomorrow'.

questions.prompt: Match negative aspect markers:

pairs.english: I do not want / like (Neg. Continuous/State)
I did not know / do not know (Neg. Completive)

questions.sentence: In relative narrative past (used in storytelling), 3rd person singular masculine 'ya' changes to '___'.
questions.explanation: In historical narration, relative past (preterite) forms carry specific tonal patterns.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Ali yana rubuta wasika' (Ali is writing a letter):
What does 'Har yanzu' mean in time reference?
questions.explanation: 'Har yanzu' means 'still' or 'even now'.

questions.prompt: Listen to the temporal sentence. What does it mean?
questions.phrase: Lokacin da na isa gida, ruwa ya dauke
options: When I arrived home, the rain had stopped
When I left home, the sun was shining
Before I reached home, rain was pouring
I stayed home until the rain started
questions.correctAnswer: When I arrived home, the rain had stopped
questions.explanation: 'Lokacin da...' = When / At the time that; 'ruwa ya dauke' = the rain stopped.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'We will learn together' in Hausa?
questions.explanation: 'Za mu' = we will; 'koya tare' = learn together.

questions.sentence: To express habitual action ('Birds fly in the sky'), Hausa uses the habitual aspect: 'Tsuntsaye ___ tashi a sama'.
questions.explanation: 'Su kan' or 'kan' expresses the habitual aspect (tend to / customarily do).

questions.prompt: What does 'Tun da' indicate in a narrative sentence?
questions.explanation: 'Tun da' signifies 'since' (e.g. 'Tun da safe' = since morning).

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Tatsuniyoyin Gizo da Hikimar Karin Magana (Spider Tales & Proverbs)
lessons.description: Explore indigenous storytelling formulas (Ga ta nan ga ta nanku), moral allegories, and timeless Hausa philosophical proverbs.

questions.prompt: Who is the legendary trickster spider at the center of Hausa oral folktales (Tatsuniyoyi)?
questions.explanation: Gizo is the famous sly trickster spider in Hausa folklore, known for his cunning wit and comical greed.

questions.prompt: Match characters in Hausa folktales with their typical traits:

questions.sentence: The traditional opening call of a Hausa storyteller is 'Ga ta ga ta nan', to which the audience responds: 'Ta zo mu ___'.
questions.explanation: The traditional call and response is: 'Ga ta ga ta nan' (Here it comes, here it is) -> 'Ta zo mu ji ta' (Let it come so we may hear it).

questions.prompt: Arrange the words of the famous proverb: 'Hankuri maganin zaman duniya' (Patience is the remedy for living in this world):
Listen to the famous Hausa proverb. What does it teach about life?
questions.phrase: Kowa ya tuna bara, ya manta bana
options: Whoever reminisces excessively about last year forgets to live in this year
Only farmers remember the dry season
A fast runner always wins the race
questions.correctAnswer: Whoever reminisces excessively about last year forgets to live in this year
questions.explanation: 'Kowa ya tuna bara, ya manta bana' warns against being trapped in the past at the expense of the present.

questions.prompt: What does the proverb 'Kaza mai 'ya'ya ba ta raba kwana da dusa' mean metaphorically?
options: A mother with children never rests from striving to provide
Chickens enjoy eating grain at night
Rich people should share with neighbors
Do not count your chickens before they hatch
questions.correctAnswer: A mother with children never rests from striving to provide
questions.explanation: The hen with chicks never sleeps away from bran/feed—a devoted caregiver never stops working for dependants.

questions.prompt: Match profound Hausa proverbs with their English meanings:

pairs.native: Zaman lafiya ya fi zama dan sarki
pairs.english: Peaceful living is better than being a prince
Education / Knowledge is the shield of humanity

questions.sentence: The traditional formula used to conclude a Hausa folktale is: 'Kunkurmin kunkus, kunkus ta ___'.
questions.explanation: 'Kunkurmin kunkus, kunkus ta kare' is the ritual signoff meaning 'The story has ended, off it goes'.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Gizo ya yaudari zaki' (Gizo deceived the lion):
What moral lesson does Gizo's character typically convey in Hausa folklore?
options: Greed, arrogance, and dishonesty ultimately bring shame and defeat
Strength is always better than intelligence
Only kings should rule the forest
questions.correctAnswer: Greed, arrogance, and dishonesty ultimately bring shame and defeat
questions.explanation: Though clever, Gizo's unbridled greed (kwadayi) always catches up with him, teaching children modesty and honesty.

questions.prompt: Listen to the proverb. What is the implied consequence?
questions.phrase: Kowa ya debi da zafi, bakinsa
options: Whoever scoops boiling hot food burns their own mouth (Reaping consequences)
Hot food should be given to travelers
A generous host cooks boiling meat
questions.correctAnswer: Whoever scoops boiling hot food burns their own mouth (Reaping consequences)
questions.explanation: 'Kowa ya debi da zafi, bakinsa' means whoever hastily takes boiling porridge will burn their own mouth—one bears the consequences of one's rash actions.

questions.prompt: Match literary folklore genres in Hausa culture:

questions.sentence: A Hausa riddle (kacici-kacici) usually begins with the phrase: 'Kacici-kacici, ka ___' (Guess what it is).
questions.explanation: 'Ka gano' means 'figure it out / discover it / guess'.

questions.prompt: Arrange the proverb: 'Duk mai rai zai dandani mutuwa' (Every living soul shall taste death):
What does the proverb 'Gani ya kori ji' emphasize?
questions.explanation: 'Gani ya kori ji' literally means 'Seeing chases away hearing'—firsthand observation supersedes hearsay.

questions.prompt: Listen to the proverb. What principle does it express?
questions.phrase: Bakin da ya ci gishiri, zai sha ruwa
options: Actions inevitably carry repercussions (Cause and effect)
Always wash your mouth before eating
questions.correctAnswer: Actions inevitably carry repercussions (Cause and effect)
questions.explanation: 'The mouth that eats salt will inevitably drink water'—you must bear the natural consequences of what you do.

questions.prompt: In Hausa riddles, what is: 'Wani abu a sama yana gudu ba kafa' (Something up in the sky running without legs)?
questions.explanation: Gizagizai (Clouds) move across the heavens without legs.

questions.sentence: Complete the proverb: 'Wanda bai san gari ba, yana kiran babba da ___'.
questions.explanation: 'Wanda bai san gari ba, yana kiran babba da yaro' (A stranger in town mistakenly addresses an elder as a child).

questions.prompt: What does 'Hikima' mean in Hausa philosophy?
questions.explanation: 'Hikima' is wisdom, sagacity, and philosophical discernment.

questions.prompt: Match moral virtues celebrated in Hausa oral literature:

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Tsarin Jumla Mai Sarƙaƙiya (Complex Syntax & Conditionals)
lessons.description: Master Hausa relative pronouns, subjunctive clauses, conditional hypotheticals, and causative/passive transformations.

questions.prompt: Which relative pronoun refers to a masculine singular antecedent ('the boy WHO came')?
questions.explanation: 'Wanda' is the masculine singular relative pronoun ('yaron da ya zo' or 'yaro wanda ya zo'). 'Wadda' is feminine singular, and 'Waɗanda' is plural.

questions.prompt: Match Hausa relative pronouns with their grammatical agreement:

questions.sentence: In conditional sentences ('If it rains, we will stay home'), Hausa pairs 'Idan' with '___': 'Idan ruwa ya yi, ___ za mu zauna a gida'.
questions.explanation: 'Idan ... to' or 'In ... to' is the standard correlative conditional construction ('If ... then').

questions.prompt: Arrange the words to say: 'Idan ka yi karatu sosai, to za ka ci jarrabawa' (If you study well, then you will pass the exam):
Listen to the passive construction. What does 'An gina...' express?
questions.phrase: An gina sabuwar asibiti a cikin garinmu
options: Passive voice: 'A new hospital was built in our town'
Future plan: 'We will build a new hospital'
Past habitual: 'They used to build hospitals'
questions.correctAnswer: Passive voice: 'A new hospital was built in our town'
questions.explanation: The impersonal/passive subject marker 'An' (or 'Aka') marks the passive voice ('An gina' = was built).

questions.prompt: How does Hausa derive a causative verb (e.g., 'to cause to enter / bring in' from 'shiga' [enter])?
questions.explanation: Adding '-r da' to the verb root creates the causative/transitive grade (grade 5): 'shiga' (enter) -> 'shigar da' (bring in / introduce).

questions.prompt: Match simple verbs with their causative (-r da) derivations:

questions.sentence: To express hypothetical unfulfilled condition ('Had I known, I would not have gone'), Hausa uses 'Da': 'Da na sani, ___ ban je ba'.
questions.explanation: Counterfactual hypothetical conditionals use 'Da ... da ...' ('Da na sani, da ban je ba').

questions.prompt: Arrange the words: 'Wannan ita ce matar da ta taimake mu' (This is the woman who helped us):
What is the function of the subjunctive particle (e.g., 'Ina son ya tafi')?
options: To express desire, necessity, or purpose in subordinate clauses
questions.correctAnswer: To express desire, necessity, or purpose in subordinate clauses
questions.explanation: The subjunctive (ya/ta/su without tense aspect auxiliaries) expresses modal subordination: wishes, commands, and intentions.

questions.prompt: Listen to the statement of necessity. What does it urge?
questions.phrase: Dole ne mu kare muhallinmu
options: It is necessary that we protect our environment
The environment is clean and safe
questions.correctAnswer: It is necessary that we protect our environment
questions.explanation: 'Dole ne...' expresses strict necessity/obligation: 'It is necessary that we protect our environment (muhalli)'.

questions.prompt: Match modal expressions of obligation and permission:

pairs.english: It is proper / appropriate / ought to

questions.sentence: To say 'Although it was late, he came', Hausa uses 'Ko da yake': '___ dare ya yi, ya zo'.
questions.explanation: 'Ko da yake' introduces a concession clause meaning 'Although / Even though'.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words: 'Aka zabi sabon shugaba' (A new leader was elected):
What does the connective 'koda shike' or 'koda yake' express syntactically?
questions.explanation: 'Ko da yake' functions as a concessive subordinator equivalent to 'although / albeit'.

questions.prompt: Listen to the sophisticated clause. What is the speaker emphasizing?
questions.phrase: Ba wai don kudi ba, sai don gaskiya
options: Not for the sake of money, but solely for truth
We spent all the money honestly
Whoever has money knows the truth
questions.correctAnswer: Not for the sake of money, but solely for truth
questions.explanation: 'Ba wai don... ba, sai don...' is an advanced rhetorical pattern: 'Not because of X, but rather for Y'.

questions.prompt: What is the meaning of 'Kada a manta' in formal discourse?
options: Lest it be forgotten / Let it not be forgotten
questions.correctAnswer: Lest it be forgotten / Let it not be forgotten
questions.explanation: 'Kada a manta' is an impersonal negative subjunctive meaning 'Let it not be forgotten / Lest we forget'.

questions.sentence: When connecting two simultaneous actions ('While he was singing, she danced'), Hausa uses: '___ yana waka, tana rawa'.
questions.explanation: 'Yayin da' or 'A lokacin da' introduces simultaneous ongoing clauses ('While / During the time that').

questions.prompt: In Hausa linguistic terminology, what is a complex sentence called?
options: Jumla mai haɗa-haɗa / Jumla mai sarƙaƙiya
questions.correctAnswer: Jumla mai haɗa-haɗa / Jumla mai sarƙaƙiya
questions.explanation: 'Jumla mai haɗa-haɗa' or 'jumla sarƙaƙƙiya' designates a complex or compound-complex sentence structure.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Tarihi da Ka'idojin Rubutun Ajami (Ajami Paleography & Orthography)
lessons.description: Explore centuries of indigenous Hausa literary tradition written in Ajami, letter modifications for ɓ, ɗ, ƙ, and text transcription.

questions.prompt: What is the historical 'Ajami' script used in Northern Nigeria?
options: Writing the Hausa language using modified Arabic script
A Latin shorthand system invented by colonial officers
questions.correctAnswer: Writing the Hausa language using modified Arabic script
questions.explanation: Ajami refers to writing indigenous African languages (such as Hausa, Fula, and Wolof) using adapted Arabic characters.

questions.prompt: Match the writing systems of the Hausa language with their historical contexts:

pairs.english: Arabic-derived script (pre-colonial to present, religious & literary poetry)
Latin-based script (introduced early 20th century, official national orthography)
Classical manuscripts and scholarly poetic commentaries in Ajami
Nigerian Naira notes featuring Ajami script for vernacular financial inclusion

questions.sentence: Because standard Arabic lacks consonants like 'ɓ', 'ɗ', and 'ts', Hausa scribes modified characters by adding ___.
questions.explanation: Scribes systematically added extra diacritic dots (e.g. 3 dots above or beneath letters) to represent unique Hausa phonemes.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words: 'Ajami tsohon rubutu ne a kasar Hausa' (Ajami is an ancient script in Hausaland):
Listen to the historical fact. Who were Danmasani and Danmarina?
questions.phrase: Wali Danmasani da Danmarina sun rubuta kasidu a Ajami
options: Renowned 17th-century Katsina scholars and poets who wrote in Ajami
questions.correctAnswer: Renowned 17th-century Katsina scholars and poets who wrote in Ajami
questions.explanation: Wali Danmasani and Danmarina were pioneer 17th-century scholars in Katsina who composed foundational poetry in Ajami.

questions.prompt: In which direction is Hausa Ajami script read and written?
questions.explanation: Like the Arabic script from which it derives, Ajami is written and read from right to left (Dama zuwa hagu).

questions.prompt: Match how Hausa vowels are represented in Ajami manuscripts:

questions.sentence: The Latin-based orthography implemented in the early 20th century in Nigeria is formally known as '___'.
questions.explanation: 'Boko' designates western/Latin script education and orthography in Hausa.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words: 'Malamai suna karanta rubutun Ajami' (Scholars read Ajami manuscripts):
Why was Ajami preserved on Nigerian currency (Naira banknotes)?
options: To allow millions of non-Western literate citizens to identify currency values
To satisfy international banks in Cairo
questions.correctAnswer: To allow millions of non-Western literate citizens to identify currency values
questions.explanation: Ajami on Naira banknotes ensures financial inclusion for citizens literate in Ajami rather than Latin Boko script.

questions.prompt: Listen to the statement. What does it say about Ajami?
questions.phrase: Rubutun Ajami babban gado ne na ilimin gargajiya
options: Ajami script is a monumental heritage of traditional scholarship
Ajami is no longer used by anyone
Ajami was brought from South America
Ajami can only be read with special glasses
questions.correctAnswer: Ajami script is a monumental heritage of traditional scholarship
questions.explanation: 'Rubutun Ajami babban gado ne na ilimin gargajiya' = Ajami is a great heritage of indigenous education.

questions.prompt: Match Hausa phonemes with their Ajami orthographic representations:

pairs.english: Represented using Arabic Ta or Sad with added diacritics
Represented using Kaf with three dots or Jim variants
Represented using Jim (ج) or Shin (ش) modified

questions.sentence: The calligraphic style most commonly used in West African and Hausa Ajami manuscripts is the ___ script.
questions.explanation: West African Ajami and Quranic manuscripts predominantly employ variants of the Maghribi / Sudani calligraphic hand.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words: 'Akwai rubuce-rubucen wakoki a Ajami' (There are written poems in Ajami):
What is the primary academic benefit of transcribing historical Ajami texts into Boko?
options: It makes centuries of historical, medical, and legal documents accessible to modern researchers worldwide
It permanently erases the original manuscripts
It proves that Hausa has no grammar
It replaces the need to teach language
questions.correctAnswer: It makes centuries of historical, medical, and legal documents accessible to modern researchers worldwide
questions.explanation: Transliteration preserves historical memory and unlocks pre-colonial African intellectual archives.

questions.prompt: Listen to the genre title. What kind of Ajami poem is this?
questions.phrase: Wakar Ya Yabon Ubangiji
options: A poem in praise of God Almighty
questions.correctAnswer: A poem in praise of God Almighty
questions.explanation: 'Wakar yabon Ubangiji' is a hymn/poem of devotion and praise of God, commonly penned in Ajami.

questions.prompt: What is an inkhorn or traditional ink called in northern manuscript culture?
questions.explanation: 'Tadawa' is traditional soot/gum ink used by scholars; 'alkalami' is the reed pen.

questions.sentence: The wooden slate used by traditional students to practice writing Ajami is called '___'.
questions.explanation: 'Allo' is the wooden tablet (slate) used by pupils to write and wash away daily texts.

questions.prompt: Which 19th-century female scholar, daughter of Usman dan Fodio, composed prolific poetry in Hausa Ajami, Fula, and Arabic?
questions.explanation: Nana Asma'u (1793–1864) was a celebrated educator, poet, and scholar who composed vital educational literature in Ajami.

questions.prompt: What is the standard formal opening salutation in an official Hausa business letter?
questions.explanation: 'Zuwa ga Mai Girma...' (To the Honorable / Respected...) is the standard formal opening in Hausa epistolary conventions.

questions.prompt: Match epistolary components in Hausa letter writing:

pairs.english: Address (top right for writer, top left for recipient in formal letters)

questions.sentence: A formal signoff formula for an official letter is: 'Ni ne naku mai biyayya, ___' (Yours faithfully / obediently).
questions.explanation: 'Ni ne naku mai biyayya' is the traditional formal closing equivalent to 'Yours obediently / faithfully'.

questions.prompt: Arrange the title: 'Neman Aikin Koyarwa a Makarantar Sakandare' (Application for a Teaching Position in Secondary School):

We regret to inform you that the meeting is cancelled
Please return my book by tomorrow

questions.explanation: 'Bayan gaisuwa mai tarin yawa da fatan alheri' is the classic polite opening formula in Hausa letter composition.

questions.prompt: What is an essay called in Hausa curriculum standards?

questions.prompt: Match essay composition genres (Nau'o'in Insha'i):

questions.explanation: 'Shimfida' (literally: laying out the carpet / foundation) is the introduction of an essay or discourse.

questions.prompt: Listen to the thesis sentence. What does it argue?
questions.phrase: Wannan matsala tana barazana ga ci gaban al'umma
options: This problem poses a threat to the development of society
Our community has solved all its problems
questions.correctAnswer: This problem poses a threat to the development of society
questions.explanation: 'Barazana' means threat; 'ci gaban al'umma' means social development.

questions.prompt: Match contemporary civic essay themes in Hausa:

pairs.english: The impact of modern information technology

questions.sentence: When writing an informal letter to an intimate friend, one addresses them warmly as: 'Zuwa ga babban ___' (To my dear friend).
questions.explanation: 'Zuwa ga babban abokina' (To my dear/great friend) is standard in informal letters (wasikar sada zumunci).

questions.prompt: Arrange the words: 'Ina rubuta wannan wasika domin sanar da kai' (I am writing this letter to notify you):

questions.prompt: Listen to the debater. What stance are they taking?
questions.phrase: Ina goyon bayan wannan batu saboda dalilai kamar haka
options: I support this motion because of the following reasons
I vehemently reject this false motion
I am neutral and do not wish to speak
The debate should be postponed till next week
questions.correctAnswer: I support this motion because of the following reasons
questions.explanation: 'Ina goyon bayan...' = I support/stand with this motion; 'dalilai' = reasons.

questions.prompt: What is 'Wasiƙar neman aiki'?
questions.explanation: 'Wasiƙar neman aiki' is an employment application letter.

questions.sentence: The core body paragraphs of an essay containing arguments and examples are termed '___ insha'i'.
questions.explanation: 'Gangar jiki' (literally: the torso / main trunk) designates the body paragraphs.

questions.prompt: Which connective should be used to introduce an opposing perspective ('On the contrary / On the other hand')?
questions.explanation: 'Akasin haka' means 'on the contrary / on the other hand'.

questions.prompt: Match formal letter expressions with English equivalents:

pairs.english: I hereby express my profound gratitude

pairs.native: Ina fatan za a duba bukatata

questions.prompt: Match classic Hausa literary works with their authors or genres:

pairs.english: Abubakar Imam's famous picaresque quest novel
Sa'adu Zungur's seminal political reform poem
Umaru Danjuma Katsina's celebrated social drama play

questions.sentence: Written poetry in Hausa is called 'Wakar rubutu', while oral sung poetry performed by bards is called 'Wakar ___'.
questions.explanation: 'Wakar baka' (oral / mouth song) denotes sung/chanted oral poetry performed with traditional instruments.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words: 'Adabi madubin rayuwar al'umma ne' (Literature is the mirror of society's life):

questions.phrase: Mamman Shata Katsina shahararren mawakin baka ne
options: The most iconic and renowned oral poet/musician in Hausa history
The first printer of newspapers in Kaduna
questions.correctAnswer: The most iconic and renowned oral poet/musician in Hausa history
questions.explanation: Mamman Shata was a legendary griot and musical philosopher awarded an honorary doctorate for his poetic contributions.

questions.prompt: What is 'Wasan kwaikwayo' in Hausa cultural arts?
questions.explanation: 'Wasan kwaikwayo' (literally: play of imitation/acting) is theatrical drama.

questions.prompt: Match traditional Hausa musical instruments with their classifications:

pairs.english: Talking drum (hourglass shaped, tension pitch drum)
Long ceremonial brass trumpet of royalty and emirs
Single-stringed plucked lute (used by Dan Maraya Jos)

questions.sentence: The metric rhythm and poetic cadence in classical written Hausa poetry is termed '___' (meter/prosody).
questions.explanation: 'Wazan' (from Arabic wazn) designates the poetic meter and syllable balance in classical verses.

questions.prompt: Arrange the words: 'Dan Maraya Jos ya shahara wajen kidan kuntigi' (Dan Maraya Jos was famous for playing the kuntigi lute):

questions.prompt: Listen to the literary analysis. What components of poetry are named?

options: Poetic verse (baiti) contains a chorus/rhyme (amshi) and meter (wazan)
Writers should not sing in public
All poems must be printed in books
questions.correctAnswer: Poetic verse (baiti) contains a chorus/rhyme (amshi) and meter (wazan)
questions.explanation: 'Baiti' is a stanza/couplet, 'amshi' is rhyme/chorus refrain, and 'wazan' is poetic meter.

questions.prompt: Match poetic terminology in Hausa literary criticism:

questions.sentence: The historic Hausa poetic chronicle of Kano kings composed across centuries is known as 'Wakar ___'.

questions.explanation: Sakkwatanci preserves distinct archaisms like /hw/ for /f/ ('hwan' for 'fara') and distinct nominal suffixes.

questions.prompt: Listen to the policy maxim. What are described as the bedrock of progress?

Building roads is the only duty of state
Money and silver surpass all wisdom

questions.sentence: When translating between English and Hausa, translating word-for-word without cultural context is called 'Fassaran kalma-da-___'.
